claims.text: On July 19, 2024, a faulty CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor content update crashed Windows machines worldwide in blue-screen loops [Source: ev-1].

The root cause was an out-of-bounds memory read in the sensor's C++ code, specifically triggered by an untrusted pointer dereference from a 21-byte input that passed a flawed content validator due to missing input validation and a memory-safety defect [Source: ev-1].

This incident affected roughly 8.5 million Windows devices globally because one security agent deployed at enterprise scale with fast-cadence updates became a global single point of failure [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: The consequences were severe across multiple sectors, including grounded airlines (with Delta cancelling approximately 7,000 flights), disruptions to banks, hospitals, 911 services, and broadcasters [Source: ev-1].
Financially, Delta incurred about $500M in costs and later sued CrowdStrike while hiring David Boies [Source: ev-1].
In the stock market, CrowdStrike shares fell by about 11% on Monday, July 22, 2024 [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, CEO George Kurtz testified before Congress on September 24, 2024 after the company apologized and promised deployment-process changes [Source: ev-1].
